method: No image model was used and nothing was generated. The shipped painting is split into two layers — the body with the eye disc erased and refilled from the body's own black, and a feathered disc holding the eye — and each of the 24 frames is an affine pose of those layers plus a colour grade. Every pixel therefore descends from the existing asset.

tool: art-department/tools/rig-spritesheet.py --enemy death-beholder (Pillow + numpy one-layer affine rig)
covers: death-beholder.preview.webp (animated flipbook, review only — not shipped)
method: No image model was used and nothing was generated. The shipped painting arrived fully opaque on black, so the black ground connected to the border is first keyed to alpha (graded from its own brightness, so the corona's spray fades out); the enclosed blacks - spines, sockets, mouth - stay opaque. The whole matted painting is then posed as one layer: each of the 24 frames is an affine pose plus a colour grade. The attack is uniform scale only: coil to 0.80 and dim, then swell to 1.14 on the very next frame. Every pixel descends from the existing asset.

tool: art-department/tools/rig-spritesheet.py --enemy green-jelly (Pillow + numpy one-layer affine rig, posed about a foot-line pivot)
covers: green-jelly.preview.webp (animated flipbook, review only — not shipped)
method: No image model was used and nothing was generated. The shipped painting arrived fully opaque on black, so the black ground connected to the border is first keyed to alpha, the same matte as the death-beholder's. The matted jelly is then posed as one layer, and every pose is taken about a pivot on its foot line (330, 548 in source pixels: the middle of the base), not about the canvas centre: it squashes along the floor and stretches upward, wider being shorter. The attack sinks to a squash (1.24 x 0.72), springs off the floor on the very next frame (0.82 x 1.24, lifted 34px) and lands spread wide toward the player. Every pixel descends from the existing asset.
